useCase.name: Mark daily attendance for a class, and correct a mark when the day turns out differently

intent.name: attendance.daily.mark
intent.summary: Save the day's attendance for a class and section, one mark per student. One step, and it is the record a parent is told from.

routesElsewhere.note: No attendance is marked on a closed day (BR-3, E2). Which days are closed is the calendar's business.

steps.note: One step. Approved leave is already applied to the roster before the teacher begins (BR-6), so a child on sanctioned leave arrives pre-marked and is not overwritten.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A closed day, a future date, an unmarked student, a section outside the actor's scope and a register already saved are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: every student's mark, the marked-by and marked-at stamps and the audit entry together or not at all (E9). The correction window runs from marked_at (BR-5). Absences feed the alert route but nothing is sent by this — a person decides when a family is told (BR-9, UC-05-09 BR-1). A student placed in the section part way through the term carries no mark for the days before their placement (BR-12).

operations.name: attendance.daily.mark
operations.idempotencyKey: section_id + date, since a section carries one daily register per date and a repeat returns ALREADY_MARKED rather than a second one
operations.purpose: Save one mark per student for a class, section and date.

parameters.name: section_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No section matches, or none assigned to the acting user.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with class, section and roster size.

parameters.notes: The section being marked. A Teacher may mark only their own assigned sections (E6).

parameters.name: date
parameters.notes: Not in the future (E3) and not an off-day or holiday (E2). Defaults to today on the screen; in a plan it comes from the request, because backdating beyond the configured window is the Coordinator's act rather than the teacher's (BR-4).

parameters.name: marks
parameters.notes: One entry per student on the roster, each with a mark. Every student carries one — a student left unmarked is not the same as a student marked present, and the difference matters when somebody asks where a child was (BR-2, E1). The marks come from what the actor stated; see PR-1.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

errors.note: A day the school was closed is not a day anybody was absent (BR-3). The calendar decides which days those are.

planningRules.rule: Report the roster and the resulting counts before the plan is emitted. "Everyone present except Bilal" asserts twenty-nine present marks the actor never said aloud, and each of those is evidence a parent may be shown (BR-2).

Never default a student to present because the request did not mention them. Unmarked and present are different facts, and the difference matters when somebody asks where a child was (BR-2) — where the request does not account for everyone, ask rather than filling the gaps.
Never mark a closed day. A day the school was shut is not a day anybody was absent (BR-3), and E2 refusing it is the calendar doing its job — never move the date to the nearest open day.

Never overwrite a pre-applied leave mark. Approved leave is applied to the roster before marking begins (BR-6) precisely so a child on sanctioned leave is not marked absent, and replacing it undoes a decision somebody made.
Never re-emit after ALREADY_MARKED. A register already saved is corrected with a reason, and the original mark stays visible (BR-7) — saving again would be a second register for one day.
Never chain an alert onto marking. Absences feed the alert route but a person decides when a family is told (BR-9), and a parent messaged automatically is one the school did not choose to message.

date comes from the request, never defaulted to today in a plan. Backdating within the window is permitted; beyond it the Coordinator marks, because a record entered a fortnight later is a different kind of claim (BR-4).

reversal.statement: A saved register is not deleted or re-saved. A wrong mark is corrected through attendance.daily.correct, with a reason, and the original stays visible alongside it — attendance is evidence, and evidence that can be quietly changed is not evidence (BR-7). The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

Leave applied after the fact updates the mark itself (UC-05-11 BR-9) — approving it is the Coordinator's act, not a correction here.

routesElsewhere.note: Where an alert has already gone, no retraction is sent — a parent told their child was absent is not told twice (BR-10, UC-05-09 BR-12).

steps.note: One step. Within the hour of saving the teacher may correct their own marks; after it, the Coordinator does — the teacher can ask, but cannot change it themselves (BR-5, BR-8).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A closed correction window, a missing reason and a section outside the actor's scope are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write: the new mark, what it was changed from, who changed it and why, together with the audit entry or not at all. Nothing is overwritten — the original mark stays visible, because attendance is evidence and evidence that can be quietly changed is not evidence (BR-7). A correction from absent to present or late suppresses an alert not yet sent, and does not send a second message where one has already gone (BR-10).

operations.name: attendance.daily.correct
operations.idempotencyKey: attendance_id + student_id + new_mark, so a repeat does not record a second correction to the same value
operations.purpose: Change one student's mark on a saved register, keeping the original visible.

parameters.name: attendance_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No saved register matches within the actor's scope.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with class, section, date and when they were marked.

parameters.notes: The saved register, resolved from the section and date the actor named.

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No student on that register matches.

parameters.name: new_mark
parameters.type: enum: Present | Absent | Late | On leave
parameters.notes: What the mark becomes. Read from what the actor stated — absent, late and on leave are three different facts about a morning.

parameters.name: correction_reason
parameters.notes: Maximum 250 characters. Required for every correction, whoever makes it (BR-7, E5). The actor's own words — attendance is evidence.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The correction, and what it replaced.

fields.name: changed_from
fields.description: The previous mark, kept alongside the new one (BR-7).

fields.name: within_teacher_window
fields.description: True where the teacher's hour had not passed (BR-5).

fields.name: alert_suppressed
fields.description: True where an alert had not yet gone and has now been stopped (BR-10).

fields.name: alert_already_sent
fields.description: True where the parent has already been told. No retraction is sent (BR-10).

errors.meaning: The teacher's correction window has passed.
errors.note: Message: "The hour for changing this has passed. Ask your Coordinator." The teacher can ask, but cannot change it themselves (BR-8).

errors.meaning: A correction was made with no reason.
errors.note: Message: "Give a reason for changing this mark." Ask; never compose one.

errors.meaning: The section is not assigned to the acting user.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the correction reason. Attendance is evidence, and a mark changed with an explanation nobody gave is a change nobody can defend (BR-7, E5).
Never treat WINDOW_PASSED as something to route around. After the hour the Coordinator corrects it (BR-8) — the teacher can ask, and asking is not something a plan does on their behalf.

Read the new mark from what the actor said, never from what would tidy the register. Absent, Late and On leave are three different facts about a morning, and On leave in particular asserts that leave was approved.

Report whether the alert had already gone. A correction from absent suppresses an unsent alert but sends no retraction where one has gone (BR-10) — the parent has been told something that is now wrong, and somebody may want to phone them.
Never correct a mark to On leave in place of approving leave. Leave applied after the fact updates the mark through its own route (UC-05-11 BR-9), with the Coordinator's decision behind it.

reversal.statement: A correction is not undone. Correcting it again is another recorded change, and every version stays visible with what it was changed from (BR-7). Where an alert has gone, no retraction follows (BR-10). The controller must not attempt a compensating call.
